Changelogs

Technical changes that affect AIVAX products, services, or the public API. Dates identify when entries were added or updated, not confirmed production rollout dates. Each item identifies the affected product or service; maintenance with no user-facing effect is omitted.

This page lists the changes from the last 14 days. Older entries are kept in the changelog archive.

Friday, November 20th, 2026 #

Changes:

  • Account — Monthly subscription model quota renewal. The monthly subscription model quota no longer resets on the 1st of each month. The quota window now starts with the first request that consumes it and lasts one month, so it renews on the monthly anniversary of the first use — a quota first used on October 15 renews on November 15. A month without any use starts no window, and long-inactive accounts get a fresh window on their next request. The resetAt time in the account balance response reflects the first-use anniversary. Existing consumption keeps its history, so accounts whose current window already started on the 1st continue on that anchor until the next renewal.
  • Models — New subscription models. Adds @aivax-subscription/qwen3.8-max, @aivax-subscription/step-5-preview, and @aivax-subscription/grok-4.7 to the subscription model catalog, joining the existing five. All plans include the same shared monthly quota; see Subscription models.
  • AI gateways — Internet access toggle for the virtual Bash tool. AI gateway settings now include an Allow internet access option for the virtual Bash tool, enabled by default. Disabling it removes network commands such as curl, wget and ping from the Bash environment so the model runs commands fully offline. Existing gateways keep internet access; the option can be changed at any time in the gateway settings.

Thursday, November 19th, 2026 #

Changes:

  • RAG — Document limits per account and per collection. Each plan now limits the number of documents stored per account and per collection: Free 2,000 per account and 1,000 per collection, Pro 200,000 and 50,000, Max 250,000 per collection with no account limit, and Ultimate 500,000 per collection with no account limit. Only creating new documents counts; updating or reindexing existing documents is not affected. When a limit is reached, document creation fails with 400 Bad Request, including through imports, MCP tools, memories, and the Media Injector. Delete documents or upgrade the plan to continue; see Plans and Limits.

Wednesday, November 18th, 2026 #

Breaking changes:

  • Models — Subscription model fields. GET /api/v1/information/models.json no longer returns pricing[].subscriptionMultiplier and now returns flags.isSubscription. In GET /v1/models, _details.provider_model.subscription_multiplier is replaced by the boolean _details.provider_model.subscription. Subscription models return empty pricing arrays. Update clients that read the removed fields to use the new ones; see Models and gateway names.
  • Audio transcriptions — Grok STT 1.0 removed. @x-ai/grok-stt-1.0 (also accepted as x-ai/grok-stt-1.0) reached end of life and is no longer available; requests that name it now fail. @x-ai/grok-stt-2.0 replaces it as the default speech-to-text model at the same price of $0.10 per hour. Update requests that name the old model to use @x-ai/grok-stt-2.0, or omit the model to use the default; see Audio transcriptions.

Fixes:

  • Speech — ElevenLabs v3 and Multilingual v2 prices. @elevenlabs/eleven-v3 and @elevenlabs/eleven-multilingual-v2 now cost $0.04 per 1,000 characters, down from $30, correcting a pricing error. The dashboard price labels for these models and GPT-4o mini TTS now match the amount charged.

  • Models — Look up models by vendor-prefixed ID. The name filter on GET /api/v1/information/models.json and the filter parameter on GET /v1/models now recognize names such as minimax-m3.1-flash for @minimax/m3.1-flash without treating flash and flash-lite as the same model.

Changes:

  • Account — Monthly subscription model quota. Pro, Max, and Ultimate now include a monthly quota for subscription models, the models whose names start with @aivax-subscription/, renewed at the start of each calendar month. Using these models never debits the account balance; other models are still charged to the balance. Free and Custom plans have no quota. When the quota is exhausted, or the plan has none, requests to subscription models return 429 Too Many Requests until it renews next month. The account balance response reports the quota as a used percentage in a subscription consumption of type InferenceMonthly, and planLimits.includesSubscriptionModels is true on plans that include it. The previous model subscription multiplier no longer applies. The new Subscription models page lists the available models, their context windows, and the usage each plan includes as an equivalent at catalog prices, and describes the dynamic consumption rate, availability, and data retention of these models. Subscription models are not zero data retention and fail when Zero data retention providers only is enabled.
  • Summarization and Extraction — PDF URLs. The provider now fetches a PDF directly when the file part has a public HTTP(S) URL whose path ends in .pdf, or a filename ending in .pdf. These downloads use the provider’s file limits. Existing request fields still work.
  • Audio transcriptions — New models and lower Parakeet price. Added @nvidia/nemotron-3.5-transcribe ($0.001 per minute, recordings up to one hour, 40 languages) and @qwen/qwen3-asr-1.7b ($0.027 per hour). @nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 now costs $0.001 per minute, down from $0.0015.
  • Speech — Speechify Simba 3.5 and updated prices. Added @speechify/simba-3.5, a text-to-speech model covering 48 languages, at $0.0075 per 1,000 characters, selectable in AI gateways, chat clients, and the dashboard. @fish-audio/drama-3 now costs $0.01 per 1,000 characters, up from $0.002, and @elevenlabs/eleven-flash-v2.5 costs $0.02, up from $0.01.

Tuesday, November 17th, 2026 #

Fixes:

  • Chat clients — Session metadata in messaging integrations. Replies and scheduled messages from WhatsApp, Telegram, and other messaging integrations now carry the session metadata to MCP servers, protocol functions, gateway workers, and stored conversations, as web chat sessions already did.
  • Gateways — Reserved MCP metadata keys. Custom metadata keys beginning with _aiv no longer make MCP tool calls fail. They are ignored, and the AIVAX fields keep their values.
  • Tools — Tool explanations no longer break MCP and protocol function calls. With tool explanations enabled, AIVAX now removes _tool_reason and _tool_goal from the arguments it sends to MCP servers and protocol function callbacks. MCP servers that reject unknown arguments no longer fail these calls. Streamed servertool events still include both fields and explanation. See Tool explanations.
  • Account — Inactive accounts with a balance are kept. Disabled or inactive accounts are no longer deleted by the scheduled cleanup while they still hold a balance.
  • Models — Model lookup with suffixes. The name filter of GET /api/v1/information/models.json now ignores a # provider tag or a : variant suffix and returns the matching base model.

Changes:

  • Models — GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol. Adds @openai/gpt-6.2-astra, @openai/gpt-6.2-astra:pro, @openai/gpt-6.2-sol, and @openai/gpt-6.2-sol:pro, with reasoning, image and file input, tool calling, and structured output. @model-router/openai:frontier now routes to @openai/gpt-6.2-astra instead of @openai/gpt-6-astra; select @openai/gpt-6-astra directly to keep the previous model.
  • Decisions — Liquid d1.2 and d1.2-ultra. Adds @liquid/d1.2 and @liquid/d1.2-ultra, with a 64K context, image input, and yes/no, multiple-choice, and score questions. @liquid/d:latest now resolves to @liquid/d1.2 instead of @liquid/d1.1. Check prices in the decision model listing.
  • Gateways — Metadata in every MCP request. AIVAX now sends the calling context and custom metadata in params._meta of every request to an MCP server, including initialize, tools/list, skills/list, and resources/read, not only tools/call. Discovery results are cached per calling context, so MCP servers may receive more discovery requests than before. See Metadata sent with MCP requests.
  • Chat clients — Reasoning and tool activity in the hosted chat. The hosted web chat now groups reasoning and tool calls into collapsible blocks with a summary such as “Thought, called web_search”. A block opens while the model is working, scrolls within a fixed height, and collapses when the answer starts; opening or closing a block by hand keeps it that way. While a tool runs, the status line shows the tool’s explanation instead of the generic thinking label. Tool results are not shown in the conversation. When Tool call visibility (showToolCalls) is off, these blocks are hidden and only the status line remains. See Publish the hosted chat and Tool explanations.

Monday, November 16th, 2026 #

Fixes:

  • Account — Top-ups paid with a saved payment method. Adding credits no longer opens an empty browser tab when a saved payment method settles the payment immediately. The dashboard confirms the payment instead.

Changes:

  • Account — Brazilian taxes on payments. New payments now include Brazilian taxes, added on top of the amount due: credit top-ups, subscription payments and renewals, and bills issued by the AIVAX team. The charged total is the amount divided by (1 - 0.1333), which corresponds to approximately 11.33% of the total in service taxes and 2% in IOF. For example, a $19.00 subscription payment charges $21.92. Taxes are not added to the balance, and listed plan prices do not include them. Before you confirm a top-up, the dashboard now lists the credits, the service fee, the taxes, and the total charged. The amount due shown for a plan change already includes taxes, and receipts list each tax. Invoices created before this change keep their amount. See Taxes on payments.
  • Account — Service invoices. When AIVAX issues a service invoice (nota fiscal de serviços) for a payment, you receive a dashboard notification and an e-mail, and the invoice gets a Service invoice download link in the Invoices tab of Analytics. Usage data returns the link in serviceInvoiceLocation, which is null until the service invoice is issued.
  • Decisions — Conversation input and media. Decision requests now accept input, an array of conversation messages, instead of state. The two fields are mutually exclusive. The conversation becomes the first state item, and image, audio, video, and document parts are evaluated as media. Models that list audioinput, videoinput, or fileinput in the decision model listing accept those parts; Gemini Decision 1 accepts all four. See Send media.
  • Routing — Auxiliary steps stay on zero data retention providers. Content moderation, the complexity router, RAG query rewriting (UserRewrite and FullRewrite), the summary read aloud by chat clients with summarizeTextBeforeAudioSynthesis, the rewrite of text with voice instructions for speech generation, and Media Injector now always run on a zero data retention provider, even when Zero data retention providers only is disabled. When none is available for one of these steps, the request fails with an error stating that no zero data retention provider is available, instead of falling back to another provider; retry later. Only content moderation still moves on to its other models. These steps can cost about twice as much as before, depending on the provider selected. See Zero data retention providers only.
  • Analytics — Cost origin and payment totals in the monthly report. The monthly report now splits the billed amount into provider costs, passed through from third-party providers, and service costs, charged directly by AIVAX. It also totals the payments confirmed in the month, with their taxes and, when available, the payment method and its fees. Get Monthly Usage Report returns these totals in providerCost, directServiceCost, and payments.
  • RAG — Reflex v1.5 reranker. The rerank endpoint accepts @aivax/reflex-v1.5, a higher-accuracy option to @aivax/reflex-v1. It ranks up to 15,000 documents per request and returns at most 50 results, so requests with a larger top_n are rejected. It costs $0.015 per 1M input tokens, and documents already processed recently for the same account cost $0.005 per 1M tokens. Requests count toward the subscription allowance, like Reflex v1. The default reranker is still @aivax/reflex-v1; select the new model with model. See Reranking.

Friday, November 13th, 2026 #

Breaking changes:

  • Chat clients — allowedFrameOrigins removed. The deprecated allowedFrameOrigins chat client option is no longer returned when you read a chat client. Requests that still send it keep working, and the value is ignored. Embedding the hosted chat in an iframe is not affected; see Publish the hosted chat.

Fixes:

  • Batch — Jobs resume after the daily item limit. A job paused because the plan’s daily limit of processed items was reached now resumes automatically after the limit window resets, as described in Batch and Agentic Tests limits. Previously, these jobs could stay paused until they were resumed manually. Jobs that are already stuck can be resumed by setting their state to active. Temporary model provider failures still pause the job after repeated errors and still require a manual resume.
  • Chat clients — Session token count after Send Prompt. Sessions that receive messages through Send Prompt now report their token count in the session listing. Previously, these sessions always showed 0 tokens. Counts are updated on the next prompt of each session.

Changes:

  • Chat clients — Insert messages into a session. The new POST /api/v1/web-chat-client/<chat-client-id>/sessions/insert-message endpoint appends user, assistant, or tool messages to an active session, identified by sessionId or tag, without running inference and without consuming balance. The inserted messages are used as context by the next prompt. The request fails with 409 while an inference is running for the session.

Thursday, November 12th, 2026 #

Breaking changes:

  • Image generation — DreamShaper 8 LCM removed. @lykon/dreamshaper-8-lcm is no longer available, and requests that name it are rejected. Choose another text-to-image model, such as @black-forest-labs/flux-schnell. See Image generation.

Changes:

  • Chat clients — Disposable context in Send Prompt. Send Prompt accepts a new context field with text or OpenAI-compatible content parts, including images, audio, video, and files. The parts are added to the beginning of the last user message for that request only and are never saved to the session history or the stored conversation. See Add disposable context to the last user message.
  • Image generation — GPT Image 2.6 Flare and Sunburst. Adds @openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare, for fast generation, and @openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst, for detailed compositions. Both support reference-image editing and are priced at $0.025 per output image plus $0.025 per reference image per output.
  • Image generation — Older models deprecated. @openai/gpt-image-2.5-flare, @openai/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst and @openai/gpt-image-1-mini are now marked as deprecated. They keep working for now; move to @openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare, @openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst or @openai/gpt-image-2.
  • Image generation — Lower prices. @bytedance/seedream-5-pro now costs $0.035 per output image, down from $0.09, and @recraft/recraft-v4.1-flash costs $0.007, down from $0.008.

Wednesday, November 11th, 2026 #

Fixes:

  • Account — Credit top-ups add the chosen amount to the balance. A new top-up now adds exactly the amount you choose to your balance. The payment processor fee and the service fee are charged with the payment and are not added to the balance. Credits already added are unchanged. See Credit top-ups.

Changes:

  • Dashboard — Redesigned home page. The dashboard home now shows your credit balance with a reminder to add credits when it runs out, usage for the last 24 hours, 7, 30, or 90 days with token and request trends, and shortcuts to AI Gateways, RAG Collections, Chat clients, and Voice. Get started, Copy Prompt, and the yearly daily token usage chart remain available. Token totals now count only token-based usage, and request totals count each request once. The code sample panel was removed; see the Overview for examples.
  • Dashboard — More consistent page layout. Section titles on the Usage page now include a short description, and section spacing on Analytics and Batch is aligned with other pages. On the Generations page, the text tools and the image and reranking tools are grouped under their own labels in the tab list.
  • AI Gateways — New tool.fetched and message.completed worker events. Gateway workers now receive tool.fetched after a server-side tool returns its result, and can keep, block, or replace that result with a tool.fetched.response action. Workers also receive message.completed after each inference finishes, with the messages, errors, whether the failure was fatal, and usage; this event is a notification and its response is ignored. Workers that return 2xx for unknown events need no change. See Gateway Workers.
  • Account — No service fee on credit top-ups for Pro, Max, and Ultimate. Adding credits on Pro, Max, and Ultimate no longer includes the AIVAX service fee. The payment processor fee still applies, and Free keeps the service fee. The dashboard shows each fee before you confirm. See Credit top-ups.
  • Account — Daily ceiling on the inference commission. The plan’s inference commission on integrated-model inference is now limited to $1.50 per day on Free, $1.20 on Pro, and $1.00 on Max. After the ceiling is reached, model inference is charged at the model’s rates until midnight in the America/Sao_Paulo time zone. Other services that include the plan multiplier in their rates are not covered by the ceiling. See Plan multipliers.
  • Account — Inference commission as a separate usage entry. For integrated-model inference, the plan’s commission is now recorded as its own usage entry, inference.commission, under the same model as the request. Token entries now show the model’s rates without the commission; the total charged for a request is unchanged while the daily ceiling has not been reached. If you calculate unit prices from usage entries, add the inference.commission entries to get the full cost.
  • Account — Model names on moderation and Agentic Tests usage. Input moderation usage is now recorded under @aivax/layered-moderation and attributed to the same resources as the request, such as the API key and AI gateway. Simulated-user and judge usage of Agentic Tests is recorded under @aivax/agentic-tests:user-<profile> and @aivax/agentic-tests:judge-<profile>, such as @aivax/agentic-tests:judge-medium, instead of the underlying model. Remote resources fetched by a test are attributed to its run. Prices are unchanged.

Tuesday, November 10th, 2026 #

Breaking changes:

  • Chat clients — New webhook URLs for messaging integrations. Telegram, Z-API, Evolution API, and Kapso integrations now have a webhook URL that contains a key generated for each integration. Copy the new URL from the integration settings in the dashboard and update it in the provider, or use Update hooks for Telegram. Current URLs keep working until December 1st, 2026 and are rejected after that date. You can rotate the key at any time with Rotate webhook key or POST /api/v1/web-chat-client/<id>/integrations/<name>/hook-key; the previous URL stops working immediately. Telegram webhooks registered with the new URL also require the secret token that Update hooks configures. See Chat clients.
  • Chat clients — Changing context goes back into the system instructions. The November 9th change is reverted: the content loaded from a session’s contextLocation and the instructions of POST /api/v1/public/chat-clients/<access-key>/prompt are again appended to the system instructions, after the session extraContext, instead of being sent as a user message after the last user message. instructions again accepts only a string or an array of strings, joined with blank lines; content parts such as images and files are no longer accepted. See Choose where to put context.
  • Chat clients — Kapso webhook signatures are verified. When Webhook secret key is set on a Kapso integration, requests whose X-Webhook-Signature doesn’t match are rejected. Leave it empty if you haven’t configured a secret in Kapso. Media attachments are now downloaded only from the Kapso API.

Fixes:

  • Chat clients — Scheduled messages keep running when an account is unavailable. Scheduled messages for other chat clients are no longer held back by a chat client whose account is disabled.
  • Chat clients — Schedule details require ownership of the chat client. Viewing or cancelling a scheduled message or recurring task now returns an error unless the chat client belongs to your account.
  • Language models — Invalid routing presets are rejected. Numeric values in routing_preset or routing_options.preset that don’t match a routing option now return a validation error instead of a server error. A numeric model # suffix that doesn’t match a routing option is now read as a provider tag.
  • Language models — Providers that can’t fit the input are skipped. Routing no longer picks a provider whose context window is known to be smaller than the request input.

Changes:

  • Data processing — Patches in instruction refinement. Each item of suggestedFixes returned by POST /api/v1/generations/instruction-refinement now has a patches array with the fix as unified diffs against the context items sent in the request, one per changed item, so you can preview and apply a fix without rewriting it by hand. patches is empty when a fix needs content or facts that aren’t in the request. Existing response fields are unchanged. See Instruction Refinement.
  • Chat clients — Longer session access keys. New chat client sessions get longer access keys. Existing keys keep working.
  • Language models — Provider names in the model catalog. The model catalog and the models endpoint now show each provider’s public name only, without internal suffixes. Provider tags are unchanged.
  • Conversations — Moderation refusals are identified in the conversation list. Conversations refused by AI gateway moderation now show a Moderated label with the violated categories in the dashboard conversation list, instead of Error. GET /api/v1/conversations returns these categories in the new moderationCategories field, which is null for conversations that moderation didn’t refuse.

Monday, November 9th, 2026 #

Breaking changes:

  • Chat clients — Changing context no longer goes into the system instructions. The content loaded from a session’s contextLocation and the instructions of POST /api/v1/public/chat-clients/<access-key>/prompt are now sent as a user message right after the last user message, instead of being appended to the system instructions. Neither is saved to the session history or returned in createdMessages, and changing them on each request no longer invalidates the prompt cache of the conversation. Models usually give user messages less weight than system instructions: if you used instructions or contextLocation for rules the assistant must always follow, move those rules to the session extraContext or the AI gateway instructions. extraContext is unchanged and stays in the system instructions. instructions now also accepts one OpenAI-compatible content part or an array of them, including images and files; strings and arrays of strings keep working, but array items are now sent as separate text parts instead of being joined with blank lines. See Choose where to put context.

Fixes:

  • Language models — Failing providers are retried and avoided. When a provider fails before it sends the first response token, including errors reported inside a streaming response, the request is now retried on another eligible provider instead of returning Provider returned error. Providers that keep failing are ranked lower by every routing preference and are temporarily removed from routing when they fail repeatedly. Requests limited by allowed_providers to a single unavailable provider can still fail; add "*" as the last item to allow a fallback. See Routing setup.
  • Dashboard — AI gateway settings show their saved values. In the AI gateway editor, Moderation mode could show Layered guardrail even when Self-assessment was saved, and the Routing preference and Communication protocol pickers opened with no option selected. The editor now shows and highlights the saved option. The saved values were not changed.

Changes:

  • Chat clients — Streaming and inference options in Send Prompt. POST /api/v1/public/chat-clients/<access-key>/prompt accepts stream: true to return server-sent events with text, reasoning and tool updates, followed by a result event with the usual response body. The new inferenceOptions object overrides reasoningEffort, renderingMode (default or textual_blocks) and toolInvocationExplanations for one request, and the new tools field adds OpenAI-compatible client-side tools that are available only for that request. Temporary provider failures that happen before any output are now retried automatically. See Sending prompts from your application.
  • Data processing — Instruction refinement. The new POST /api/v1/generations/instruction-refinement endpoint reviews system instructions, prompts, skills, tool descriptions and knowledge against prompt engineering guidelines from model vendors’ documentation. The micro view reviews the wording of each item, and the macro view reviews how the items work together as one agent: purpose, limits of authority, where each rule lives, skill selection and configured capabilities. It returns an overall score, a summary, prioritized findings with the line and column range of the affected text and the guideline sources behind them, and suggested fixes. See Instruction Refinement. Requests are billed in processing units, and each context item counts as one document toward the document-processing rate limit.

Sunday, November 8th, 2026 #

Changes:

  • Dashboard — Cached input share on Conversations. The Conversations list has a new Cached % column showing how much of each conversation’s input was served from the prompt cache. For conversations with more than 1K input tokens, the value is green above 95%, yellow above 90%, and shows a warning below that. A dash means no cached input was reported, which usually means the model or provider doesn’t support prompt caching. GET /api/v1/conversations now also returns cachedInputTokenCount.
  • Dashboard — BYOK usage in Analytics. Usage per model in Analytics now includes models used through AI gateways with your own provider key (BYOK). BYOK cost is an estimate based on the catalog price of the matching AIVAX model and is never charged; BYOK models with no catalog match show their tokens with no cost. The new Effective usage column shows the amount actually charged, and models used both ways show the AIVAX share of their tokens on hover. Past BYOK usage is estimated from stored conversations, so it only covers conversations that were kept. Balance, period spend, invoices, and monthly reports are unchanged.

Saturday, November 7th, 2026 #

Changes:

  • Language models — Higher prices on Grand Anak routes. Requests served by the grand-anak-<route> special providers now cost twice the previous token rates for input, cached input, and output. Other providers are not affected. Check current rates in GET /api/v1/information/models.json, and remove these tags from allowed_providers or use the Balanced preference to keep requests off special providers. See Special providers.

Friday, November 6th, 2026 #

Breaking changes:

  • Account — Lower Pro and Max limits. Pro and Max now have lower rate limits, storage, retention, and daily allowances. Max has fixed limits where it previously had none, a 10 GB storage quota with excess at $0.30/GB/month, 14-day conversation retention, and a 1.02x inference commission multiplier. Pro integrated model requests are 150/min and Pro search history is kept for 3 days. Review the new values in Plans and limits and pace requests that could now return 429 Too Many Requests.
  • Language models — Special provider routes renamed. Each special provider route now has its own name and routing tag, such as Grand Anak (Cyan Route) with the tag grand-anak-cyan. The previous tags grand-anak, grand-anak-flex, and grand-anak-route-<n> no longer match any provider. If allowed_providers, an AI gateway’s Allowed providers, or a #tag model suffix lists one of them, replace it with a current tag from GET /api/v1/information/models.json. See Special providers.

Fixes:

  • RAG — Collection tags update immediately. The tags returned in collection details now reflect added, edited, and deleted documents right after the change, instead of possibly showing an earlier list for a few minutes.

Changes:

  • Models — LFM3-1.7B and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 abliterated. Adds @liquid/lfm-3-1.7b, a compact reasoning model with tool calling and structured output, and @deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-abliterated, an uncensored variant of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 with tool calling and image input.
  • Dashboard — Avi Assistant conversations are not stored. Conversations with the Avi Assistant in the dashboard no longer appear on the Conversations page. Usage and billing records are still created.
  • Account — Ultimate plan. A new Ultimate plan is available at $199 per month. It keeps the limits previously offered by Max: no plan limit on integrated model requests, BYOK requests, or new Agentic Test runs, 20 GB of storage, 30-day retention, a 1.00x inference commission multiplier, and dedicated support. GET /api/v1/information/plans.json now also returns Ultimate. See Plans and limits and subscription pricing.
  • Docs — Plan limits on one page. Every per-plan limit, including RAG, data processing, speech, built-in tools, Batch, and Agentic Tests, is now listed in Plans and limits. Product pages link to it instead of repeating the values. The page also gives approximate PU and token sizes for common content, such as scanned PDFs, web pages, and RAG queries; see Estimating PUs and tokens.
  • Dashboard — Plan comparison with Ultimate. The Plan page in My account compares Free, Pro, Max, and Ultimate side by side, with list prices loaded from the public plan list.
  • Dashboard — Faster switching between saved accounts. Switching to a saved account reuses its active console session when it is still valid, so the console no longer signs in again or asks for a two-factor code in that case. When the session has expired, the regular sign-in runs.
  • Docs — Inference pipeline pages. The Inference section has new pages for Processing pipeline, with the order in which gateway steps run and how they affect each other, Moderation, Context truncation, and Function interpreter. The previous standalone Processing pipeline page now redirects to the new one. The function interpreter (knownToolHandlerName) is now documented as deprecated; use a model with native tool calling instead.
  • Dashboard — Warning before discarding unsaved edits. Editors for AI gateways, chat clients and their integrations, skills, Agentic Tests, Batch workflows, documents, and collection settings now ask for confirmation before you leave the page with unsaved changes, including through the browser back button, a reload, or closing the tab. The same applies when a dialog with a text or code field has been edited and is still open. Saving the page, or confirming or closing the dialog, clears the warning.
  • Dashboard — Clearer two-factor code fields. The six code fields in the two-factor dialog are larger, show a placeholder dot in each empty field, highlight filled fields, and are centered in the dialog. The code is submitted as soon as all six digits are typed or pasted, and pressing Enter also confirms it.
  • Dashboard — Budget model for AI-assisted edits. The panel for editing content with AI now preselects @model-router/openai:budget, and the panel is wider so all of its options fit. You can still choose another model before requesting the edit.
